comparison: Both evaluate AlphaFold computational predictions (C43-C52) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes validation by Agadir predictions and experimental data (SAXS, ESR). Peer reviewers accept predictions as foundational and note they provide 'novel and fundamental insight.' Both treat computational predictions as well-validated by subsequent experiments.

Both evaluate FRQ purification methodology (C55-C64) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details validation by SDS-PAGE, SEC-MALS, and mass spectrometry. Peer reviewers explicitly praise this as 'a valuable advancement' overcoming previous purification challenges. Complete agreement on technical achievement and biological relevance.

Both evaluate oligomeric state and conformational properties (C65-C73) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes SEC-MALS and SAXS Kratky analysis. Peer reviewers accept findings as 'high quality' and note conclusions are 'sufficiently circumspect' given low-resolution data. Complete agreement on phosphorylation effects.

Both evaluate cw-ESR data on regional heterogeneity (C74-C86) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details quantification by δ values and site-specific effects. Peer reviewers affirm findings demonstrate 'ordered core and disordered periphery' consistent with prior proteolysis studies. Complete agreement on structural insights.

Both evaluate DEER distance constraints (C87-C95) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges low modulation depths as limitation but validates core-periphery model. Peer reviewers accept data as 'high quality' with appropriately qualified conclusions. Complete agreement despite technical challenges.

Both evaluate FFC reconstitution (C96-C102) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details validation by SEC, SDS-PAGE, and SAXS. Peer reviewers treat FFC characterization as key achievement enabling mechanistic studies. Complete agreement on complex formation and stoichiometry.

Both evaluate DEER data on FFC spatial organization (C103-C116) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative distance distributions and control experiments. Peer reviewers affirm FRQ organizes CK1 and FRH in close proximity. Both accept FRQ as organizing scaffold, though OpenEval notes WCC-binding speculation.

Both evaluate computational LLPS predictions (C117-C127) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes validation by experimental LLPS demonstration. Peer reviewers affirm conservation across species and note this contributes to 'conceptual shift in the field.' Complete agreement on LLPS propensity predictions.

Both evaluate experimental LLPS demonstration (C128-C136) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details turbidity, microscopy, and phase diagrams. Peer reviewers provide 'solid evidence' assessment and note 'bearings on mechanistic understanding.' Complete agreement on differential p-FRQ vs np-FRQ behavior.

Both evaluate live-cell imaging (C137-C141) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates functional tagging and acknowledges technical challenges. Peer reviewers affirm 'biological significance' and accept physiological expression levels. Complete agreement on in vivo FRQ condensates despite Drosophila comparison differences.

Both evaluate FRH/CK1 recruitment to condensates (C142-C146) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes specificity via CheY negative control. Peer reviewers accept FRQ 'encapsulates' partners within droplets. Complete agreement on specific recruitment mechanism controlling protein availability.

Both evaluate LLPS effects on CK1 activity (C147-C153) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details phosphorylation assays and cw-ESR rigidification. Peer reviewers strongly support findings linking LLPS to 'diminishing CK1 activity.' Complete agreement on LLPS-dependent activity modulation.

Major divergence: OpenEval rates temperature compensation role (C204-C210) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation and lack of direct in vivo evidence. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly highlighting this as 'highly intriguing' key implication. Peer reviewers more accepting of mechanistic proposal than OpenEval.

Both address conservation of LLPS in circadian clocks (C127 overlap). OpenEval in R8 evaluates computational predictions as SUPPORTED but notes speculation. Peer R14 affirms broader conservation conclusion and 'conceptual shift.' Peer reviewers more enthusiastic about conservation implications.

Both address conservation theme (C214 overlap). OpenEval R21 evaluates synthesis as SUPPORTED with appropriate qualification. Peer R14 emphasizes 'important biochemical and biophysical data' contributing to field shift. Agreement on significance with peer reviewers highlighting broader impact.

Minimal overlap (C3-C4 abstract claims). OpenEval R23 evaluates abstract summary as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 focuses on computational predictions. Both accept foundational claims but address different scopes.
Minimal overlap (C59 purification). OpenEval R24 evaluates technical achievement as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 praises purification protocol. Complete agreement on significance of methodological advance.

OpenEval R14 evaluates integrative structural conclusions (C157-C163) as SUPPORTED, synthesizing SAXS, DEER, and ESR data. No corresponding focused peer evaluation found, though findings are implicitly accepted in other peer results.

OpenEval R15 evaluates phosphorylation effects on structure (C164-C171) as SUPPORTED with detailed biophysical evidence. No corresponding focused peer evaluation, though peer reviewers accept these findings in context of other results.
OpenEval R16 evaluates oligomeric state regulation (C172-C176) as SUPPORTED, noting speculation about cellular LLPS. No corresponding focused peer evaluation found.

OpenEval R17 evaluates IDP classification and LLPS conservation (C177-C182) as SUPPORTED with some speculation. No corresponding focused peer evaluation, though conservation theme appears in peer R14.
OpenEval R18 evaluates mechanistic explanation for phosphorylation-LLPS relationship (C183-C186) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding focused peer evaluation found.
OpenEval R19 evaluates in vivo imaging with technical caveats (C187-C193) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address this in R10 but OpenEval R19 provides more detailed technical discussion.
OpenEval R20 evaluates speculative proposals about FRQ function and nuclear transport (C194-C201) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct evidence. No corresponding focused peer evaluation found.
